newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end up, bellies off highs.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end up, bellies off highs.

text.p: CME hog futures posted sharp closing gains, buoyed by short covering while pork belly futures closed higher but off best levels on pre-report evening of positions, traders said.
Hog futures closed 1.075 to 0.025 cent per lb higher with June up most and April up 0.625 at 72.700 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.225 to 2.250 higher with March up 1.450 at 74.625 cents.

Hogs rallied on short covering as traders corrected from oversold status amid expectations that cash hog prices may firm. Spillover from a sharp rally in cattle trading pits reinforced the rally in hogs with June leading the advance on buy stops, traders said.

Cash hog prices may firmer as producers were seen resisting the recent drop in cash prices that put some markets under $50 per cwt. However, resistance was still evident in April on the climb in futures because of a continued weak tone to cash pork values. Pork prices need to turn fully higher before a substantial rally can take place in cash hogs, traders said.
Rand Financials and E.D.&F. Man bought April late, traders said, and R.J. O'Brien bought June and Rosenthal Collins bought July.
In hog options, commission houses sold April 70 puts and bought 74 calls. There was also buying of June 78 calls, seen as profit taking, pit sources added.

Pork bellies ran up for sharp gains around midsession on reports of increased user interest for cash pork which added to short covering that developed following the recent sharp setback in futures prices, traders said.
"Product found some user interest at the 65-cent level," said Chuck Levitt, livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
But futures slipped at the close as traders squared positions ahead of the weekly storage report, traders said.

There was still concern that stocks have risen to levels above a year ago at CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago. Also, estimates pointed to the monthly USDA Cold Storage report showing rising stocks, they said.

After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement at warehouses outside Chicago of 1.667 million lbs, above the high end of trade estimates at 1.3 million lbs. This could weigh on belly futures Thursday and offset the expected strength from firming cash belly values, some sources noted.
"We have more bellies in storage now than a year ago. At least that is the way it would appear from the visible stocks," Levitt added.

Analyst expectations on Friday's monthly USDA Cold Storage Report ranged from 39.7 million to 43.2 million lbs in frozen storage compared with 46.5 million last year. Although stocks were seen below last year, they likely rose during the month compared with a 10-year average decline of 130,000 lbs, analysts said.
